findings.title: Denial cache short-circuits before the DB fallback, so a cached denial can keep hiding a newly granted permission
findings.body: The denial cache is checked first in Check and returns deny immediately, before the cached-permission lookup and the DB fallback that this PR adds. A denial is written with a 30s TTL (shortCacheTTL) whenever the DB result is not allowed. If a user is checked on a resource before its permission row exists (for example, a dashboard or folder just created by that user, or a frontend poll), the denial is cached for 30s. Once the permission is written, every Check for that same user/action/name/folder returns false until the entry expires, which is the exact symptom this PR is meant to fix. The denial entry should be bypassed or invalidated when the permission is granted, or the check should go to the DB before trusting a denial. At minimum this trade-off needs to be documented and covered by a test.

findings.title: Denial cache key concatenates unescaped fields, so distinct requests can collide
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey joins userUID, action, name and parent with '_' and no escaping. Different tuples produce the same key: name "a_b" with empty parent and name "a" with parent "b" both yield "...._a_b_" / "...._a_b"-style collisions. The key also shares the "perm_" prefix with userPermCacheKey. A collision makes a denial for one resource apply to another, so an unrelated resource is wrongly denied until the TTL expires. Use a separator that cannot appear in the fields (or a hash of a structured tuple).
